title: First-order proofs and theories: derivability and soundness
summary: Finite proofs with quantifiers and equality, fresh witnesses, and the distinction between proving a sentence and finding a model.
abstract: If every object with a property has another property, then finding one object with the first property should give an object with the second. A first-order proof makes this familiar argument precise without choosing a particular structure. Quantifier rules let us use an arbitrary object or a temporary witness, but they restrict what can be assumed about it and where its name may appear. These restrictions ensure that every conclusion holds in every model of the assumptions. A theory is consistent when these rules cannot produce a contradiction. Even a proof from infinitely many axioms uses only finitely many of them, including finitely many instances of any axiom schema.
